title: Quarterline SEED India evaluation dataset (design-time draft)
caveats: DESIGN-TIME DRAFT: no India retrieval index, ingestion, or grounding exists yet. These rows are retrieval and grounding cases designed NOW against real acquired documents so the future index is held to them from day one. Nothing here is scored today.

All question rows are draft_status=draft and reviewed=false; no draft may claim review. This file deliberately does NOT load through quarterline.eval.dataset.load_dataset (extra fields, unreviewed rows, and this meta line).

Spans are pending ingestion: every relevant_evidence entry carries start_offset=null and end_offset=null with offsets_pending_ingestion=true. Each span DOES carry an anchor that was verified in this session against the exact source file named in source_document. Fill offsets and run a verify_spans-equivalent after India ingestion (IND-3).

Every referenced document is real and sha256-recorded in tests/fixtures/india/manifest.json (IND-1). Periods used: Q1 FY2026-27 (2026-04-01..2026-06-30), Q4 FY2025-26 (2026-01-01..2026-03-31), and FY2025-26 annual (2025-04-01..2026-03-31). No accession ids, dates, or documents are invented.
expected_answer_hint values were parsed from the named sources (cross-checked against data/india_reconciliation.csv where available) and are UNVERIFIED BY A HUMAN.
Company-IR PDFs are cached under storage/raw/india/ but are not committed fixtures; rows citing them become answerable only after a PDF ingestion milestone.
Style: no em dashes; monetary hints give exact rupees plus the as-filed crore display string (1 crore = 10000000 rupees).
Per-question rationale, category coverage, and source ambiguities live in docs/india_eval_draft_notes.md.

expected_answer_hint: ExceptionalItemsBeforeTax = -12890000000 rupees (minus Rs 1,289 crore before tax); profit before exceptional items and tax of 412840000000 rupees (Rs 41,284 crore) reduced by the exceptional item gives reported profit before tax of 399950000000 rupees (Rs 39,995 crore); values cross-checked in data/india_reconciliation.csv, unverified by a human
notes: Exceptional-item sign semantics: the instance files the exceptional item as a NEGATIVE number (a loss or expense), so 41,284 minus 1,289 equals 39,995. Failure modes guarded: sign-flipping the item into a Rs 1,289 crore gain; quoting ProfitBeforeExceptionalItemsAndTax as reported profit before tax; or booking the annual exceptional to Q4 (the Q4 quarter context carries ExceptionalItemsBeforeTax = 0 per data/india_reconciliation.csv, so the annual exceptional arises in earlier quarters of FY2025-26 and must not be presented as a Q4 event).

question: What was Infosys' operating cash flow for Q1 FY27 (the quarter ended 30 June 2026)?

the NSE Q1 FY2026-27 consolidated instance carries zero cash-flow concepts (its facts are P&L, EPS, OCI, segments, and identifiers only)

pointer: quarterly cash flow exists only in the company-IR condensed financial statements, storage/raw/india/infosys/q1_fy2026-27/consol-fy27-q1-finstatement.pdf page 6 (net cash generated by operating activities Rs 9,330 crore)
never present the annual Rs 33,986 crore as a quarterly figure
notes: THE essential India case. Correct behavior: an insufficient-evidence response that states the figure is not present in the ingested exchange source AND points to where quarterly cash flow DOES exist. Infosys is the documented exception that publishes quarter-granularity cash flow, but only in company-IR condensed statements: consol-fy27-q1-finstatement.pdf page 6 reports net cash generated by operating activities of Rs 9,330 crore vs Rs 7,632 crore in the year-ago quarter (docs/india_source_audit.md section 5; docs/india_financial_methodology.md rule 4). Failure modes guarded: (1) fabricating a quarterly number; (2) relabeling the FY2025-26 annual CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities of 339860000000 rupees (Rs 33,986 crore, context FourD 2025-04-01..2026-03-31 in the Q4 filing) as a quarterly figure; (3) answering with the P&L profit for the period (Rs 7,775 crore), which is profit, not cash flow. Empty gold-evidence list by design, mirroring the US dataset's unanswerable rows.

expected_answer_hint: 482110000000 rupees exactly, displayed as Rs 48,211 crore at the declared presentation scale (equivalently 4,821,100 lakh); the stored value is full rupees and is never the bare number 48,211; value cross-checked in data/india_reconciliation.csv, unverified by a human
notes: Lakhs/crores normalization trap (docs/india_financial_methodology.md rule 1): the instance stores full rupees while LevelOfRounding=Crores describes presentation only. Failure modes guarded: reading the stored value as already-scaled crores (answering 48,211 rupees); applying the crore multiplier a second time to an already-rupee value (4,821,100,000,000,000); or confusing lakh with crore (Rs 48,211 lakh would be 4,821,100,000 rupees, a factor of 100 smaller than the correct 482,110,000,000). Exact integer arithmetic only; no float rounding.

per-share values never inherit a lakh or crore multiplier

expected_answer_hint: 19.17 rupees per share, exactly as filed (basic EPS is 19.19); per-share facts live in unit INRPerShare and the crore rounding scale never applies to them; value cross-checked in data/india_reconciliation.csv, unverified by a human
notes: Per-share exemption trap (docs/india_financial_methodology.md rule 1): document-level scale hints (LevelOfRounding=Crores, or Rs in Crores headers on rendered pages) must never scale EPS; 19.17 must not become 19.17 crore or 191,700,000. Guards the classic pipeline bug of applying one document-level scale to every numeric fact, including per-share units. The fact's decimals=INF (exact per-share value) vs decimals=-7 on money facts is itself the machine-checkable tell.
